correctness.rationale: The known graph has one part of size 2n-2 and n parts of size two, with a two-element cyclicizer in Dic_n. For any graph mate H, the cyclicizer lemma gives |Cyc(H)| dividing each finite cyclicizer size; a small part gives c|(c+2), so c is 1 or 2. If c=1, the large cyclicizer class has size 2n-1 and, because all of its pairs generate cyclic groups, Lemma 2.1(2) makes it a finite locally cyclic subgroup; then 2n-1 would divide |H|=4n-1, impossible. Thus c=2 and |H|=4n. The large class plus Cyc(H) is cyclic of order 2n and index two. Each small class plus Cyc(H) is cyclic order four, so every outside element has square equal to the unique nontrivial cyclicizer element z. If K=<a> is the index-two cyclic subgroup and x is outside, (xk)^2=x^2=z for every k in K; normality of K yields xkx^{-1}=k^{-1}. With x^2=a^n this is exactly the dicyclic presentation. The verifier's finite examples corroborate the graph input only.

evidence: The multipartite graph forces candidate cyclicizer size c to divide c+2, hence c is 1 or 2.

The c=1 alternative is eliminated by the large cyclicizer class and Lagrange divisibility; c=2 then forces a cyclic index-two subgroup of order 2n and order-four outside elements sharing the unique involution.

Using the cyclicizer-subgroup lemma closes the otherwise implicit point that each complete nonneighbor class plus the cyclicizer is actually a finite locally cyclic subgroup; the index-two action is then inversion.
